media.title: Paris Years — document gallery
media.description: Document gallery for Kaper’s Paris years, 1933–1934. It brings together French and European press documentation, materials relating to French film work, two distinct photographs from the November 1933 reception for Jan Kiepura, and a Paris hotel context image.
media.altText: Gallery card for Bronisław Kaper’s Paris years, combining press items, posters and contextual materials.
media.publicCaption: Gallery of press items, posters and contextual materials relating to Bronisław Kaper’s Paris years and his work in French cinema and theatrical culture, 1933–1934.
media.rightsNote: This gallery has no single rights status. Each member medium carries its own public-domain, licensed, restricted or unresolved-copyright statement; reuse must be assessed item by item.
media.publicCreditLine: Item-level credits identify the holding institution and source for every gallery member.

media.description: Advertisement for Hôtel Le Château Frontenac, 54 rue Pierre Charron, Paris 8e, used as a historical context image for Kaper’s Paris years.
media.altText: Black-and-white advertisement showing the exterior of Hôtel Le Château Frontenac at 54 rue Pierre Charron in Paris.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared, and the one fact that would settle them is missing. The advertisement reproduces a photograph of the hotel, so there is a protected subject, but neither this record nor the Gallica object cited gives a date of publication — and the date decides the question. An anonymous French work published in 1931 or later still carries restored United States copyright today; one published in 1930 or earlier does not, either because the French term had lapsed before 1 January 1996 or because the restored ninety-five-year term has since run out. Gallica supplies the digitised page under conditions governed by French law, which exclude documents protected by a third party’s copyright and leave reuse in another country to the user. Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France. The image stays on detail pages until the date is established.
